Pāṇini
grammarian. date assigned 700 B. C. or 400 B. C.
Also known a. Āhika, Śālaṅki; called Dākṣīputra a. his mother belonged to Dakṣagotra, an. Śālāturīya a. he hailed from Śālātura (Lahur); codified Sanskrit grammar; for traditional accounts of his life see Rājaśekhara's Kāvyamīmām3sā, Āryamañjuśrīmūlakalpa, Kṣemendra's Bṛhatkathāmañjarī an. Somadeva's Kathāsaritsāgara.
See K. V. Abhyankar, Dict. of Skt. Gr. GOS. edn. p.. 229-30.
For a detailed bibliography an. survey on Pāṇini an. his works see G. Cardona, Pāṇini, A Survey of Research, Motilal Banarsidass, Delhi, 1980.
For a. account of his life an. works see S. K. Belvalkar, Systems of Skt. Gr. p.. 12-28; Yudhisthira Mimamsak, Sam3skṛta Vyākaraṇ Śāstra kā Itihās Pt. I, p.. 73-231; also V. S. Agrawala, India a. known to Pāṇini, p.. 1-14; for a discussion on the probable date of Pāṇini see G. Cardona, op. cit. p.. 260-62.
For Pāṇini a. grammarian see Mahavir, Pāṇini a. Grammarian with Special Reference to Compound Formations, [Page013-b] Bharatiya Vidya Prakashan, Delhi, 1978; also Paul Kiparsky, Pāṇini a. a Variationist, CASS. class B. no. 6, Poona, 1980.
--Aṣṭādhyāyī or Pāṇinisūtra or Aṣṭaka or Pāṇinīyāṣṭaka.
See NCC. I. Revised edn. p.. 468b-72b.
